scenes.narration: Next time you fly, look at your window. See that tiny *hole* near the bottom? Why would anyone drill a hole... in a plane window?
At thirty-five *thousand* feet? Sounds like a terrible idea, right? <chuckles> Relax. It's actually there to keep you safe.
Okay, so here's the thing. As the plane climbs, the air outside gets *thinner*. Way up there, it's only about a *quarter* of what you breathe on the ground.
But the cabin keeps its air thick, so you can breathe easy. And all that air *pushes* outward on the window, really hard.
Now, your window isn't one sheet. It's *three*. The hole is in the middle one, so the whole push lands on the strong *outer* pane.
And the middle pane just waits. It's the *spare*, in case the outer one ever cracks. <short pause> So that little hole isn't a weak spot. It's the backup plan.
So next time you're on a flight and you spot it, that's your little 'oh, that's why' moment.
